title: Hormuz Ship Attacks Hit Record High As US Weighs Post-Midterm Strikes On Iran
excerpt: October recorded 28 attacks around the strait while transits topped 30 a day, and Washington warned Gulf allies to prepare for a possible short, intense campaign after November 3.
body:
• October has recorded 28 confirmed and reported ship attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz, the highest monthly total since the US-Israeli war with Iran began on February 28.
  • Traffic still moves through the US-facilitated southern route at more than 30 transits a day, about 90 percent of them tankers, according to INTERTANKO.
  • The United States has warned Gulf allies to prepare for a possible short, intense campaign against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, though President Donald Trump has not made a final decision.
  • Iran has warned of retaliation against US bases and regional economic targets, while claims about mines and the scale of attacks remain disputed.

Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz reached a record high in October, even as more than 30 vessels a day continued to transit the waterway and Washington warned Gulf allies to prepare for a possible new round of strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections on November 3.

October has seen the highest number of ship attacks on record, according to Noam Raydan, a senior fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, who has recorded 28 confirmed and reported attacks in October and 113 since February 28. The tally broadly aligns with the International Maritime Organization, which recorded 120 incidents in the strait and the wider Middle East since the conflict began, Reuters reported. More than 30 very large crude carriers were damaged, including 11 in October alone.

Shipping continues under attack

Traffic has not stopped. Vessels continue to use the southern US-facilitated route through the strait, with daily transits averaging more than 30 ships and tankers accounting for approximately 90 percent of movements, according to INTERTANKO's weekly update reported by Safety4Sea. The association said several ships had been attacked in recent incidents, with only a few minor injuries among seafarers.

"The tally broadly aligns with the International Maritime Organization, which recorded 120 incidents in the strait and the wider Middle East since the conflict began, Reuters reported ."

Reuters reported that more tankers came under attack as shipowners became increasingly willing to load cargoes inside the Gulf, lured by daily freight rates exceeding $1 million and steeper discounts offered by regional producers. Between October 5 and October 11, a dozen ships were attacked, the highest weekly number since the conflict began, according to Greece-based consultancy Marisks.

Disputed claims over mines and attacks

What happened in specific incidents remains contested. INTERTANKO said no credible evidence had emerged to support Iranian claims that vessels had struck mines, and questioned Iranian figures for the number of ships attacked. Iran, citing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, claimed seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged overnight on October 22, four during oil transfers and three after striking naval mines, Marine Insight reported, noting the Associated Press could not independently confirm the claims and UKMTO had not reported them. Trump accused Iran on Truth Social of making up reports of attacks and mines to push up oil prices ahead of the midterms, and claimed more oil was passing through the strait than before the conflict began. Iran warned US bases could be targeted if Washington continued helping commercial ships transit the strait.

Washington prepares options after the vote

The United States has told several Gulf Arab countries to prepare for a possible short, intense military campaign after the midterms, The Wall Street Journal reported. Trump has not decided, but is leaning toward a large post-election attack that could target Iranian infrastructure and nuclear sites, and has said he will not attack before November 3. Preparations include moving a Patriot missile defence system from Texas, restocking munitions, readying bomber and fighter aircraft, and an additional carrier strike group poised to join roughly 20 other US warships. INTERTANKO separately noted a third US carrier battle group is expected in early November, without clarity on whether it is a routine replacement or an increase ahead of a possible resumption of hostilities. Trump said last week the US could carry out another limited version of the spring bombing campaign, known as Epic Fury, unless Iran agrees to a deal.

Iran has warned it would respond with strikes on economic and civilian targets across the region, as it did earlier in the war against US bases, energy facilities and airports, and retains hundreds to thousands of missiles, the Journal reported. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran remained open to talks but was ready to defend itself, Marine Insight reported. Regional mediators are trying to revive negotiations, with little progress so far. For India and other large oil importers, the risk is factual and direct: the strait carried about one-fifth of world oil supplies before the war, and sustained attacks raise freight and insurance costs even while crude keeps moving. What happens next turns on the midterm outcome, the diplomacy that follows, and whether the post-election preparations become orders.

nri_angle: The Strait of Hormuz carries a large share of the crude India imports and of Gulf energy flows that affect fuel prices, freight costs and remittance-linked Gulf economies where millions of Indians work; a post-midterm escalation would be felt directly in Indian household fuel costs and Gulf shipping jobs.
